opportunity.name: GitHub Copilot Extension Distribution via DeepSeek
opportunity.summary: Build and publish Copilot Extensions that leverage DeepSeek for specialized developer workflows, distributed through GitHub's extension marketplace.

answers.a: Copilot Extensions are third-party plugins that extend GitHub Copilot's capabilities, allowing agents to integrate custom AI models, tools, or APIs directly into the IDE chat interface.

Extensions use the Copilot Extension API: a webhook endpoint receives chat requests from Copilot, processes them via a backend (e.g., DeepSeek API), and returns responses. The extension is registered via a GitHub App with the 'Copilot Extension' permission.

answers.q: Can you build a Copilot Extension that calls DeepSeek?
answers.a: Yes. The extension backend can call DeepSeek's API (e.g., deepseek-chat model) using standard HTTP requests. The extension receives user prompts, forwards them to DeepSeek, and returns the response.

Extensions are listed on the GitHub Marketplace under 'Copilot Extensions' category (https://github.com/marketplace/category/copilot-extensions). They also appear in the VS Code Copilot chat extension panel.

answers.q: Revenue model — can you charge for a Copilot Extension?
answers.a: Yes. Extensions can be sold as paid plans on GitHub Marketplace (monthly subscription). GitHub takes a 5% transaction fee. Pricing is set by the developer (e.g., $5–$20/user/month).

answers.q: How many Copilot users exist (latest numbers)?
answers.a: As of 2026, GitHub Copilot has over 2 million paid users (Microsoft Q2 2026 earnings report). Total users including free tier: ~5 million.

answers.q: Discovery — how do users find extensions?
answers.a: Users discover extensions via GitHub Marketplace search, VS Code Copilot chat extension panel recommendations, GitHub blog posts, and community forums.
Existing extensions include: 'CodeRabbit' (AI code review), 'Snyk' (security scanning), 'GitHub Actions' (CI/CD), 'StackBlitz' (instant dev environments). No major DeepSeek-powered extensions yet.

designs.name: Multi-Perspective Code Review
designs.description: An extension that analyzes pull requests from multiple angles: security, performance, maintainability, and style. Uses DeepSeek to generate separate reviews per perspective and a summary.
designs.implementation: Backend receives PR diff via Copilot chat, calls DeepSeek with structured prompts for each perspective, returns formatted review.

designs.name: Architecture Decision Recorder
designs.description: An extension that captures and documents architecture decisions (ADRs) from chat discussions. Uses DeepSeek to extract context, rationale, and consequences.
designs.implementation: Listens to Copilot chat, triggers on keywords like 'decision', calls DeepSeek to generate ADR in markdown, saves to repo.

designs.name: Technical Debt Analyzer
designs.description: An extension that scans codebases for technical debt indicators (e.g., TODOs, deprecated patterns, complexity). Uses DeepSeek to prioritize and suggest fixes.
designs.implementation: Backend receives file paths from chat, runs static analysis, calls DeepSeek to generate debt report with severity and refactoring suggestions.
designs.capital: $10,000 (server, DeepSeek API credits, static analysis tools)

cli_development.feasibility: Yes, everything can be developed and published via CLI.
cli_development.tools: GitHub CLI (gh), Node.js/npm, DeepSeek API, GitHub App creation via API, Marketplace publishing via GitHub API.
steps: Create GitHub App with Copilot Extension permission using `gh api`
Set up webhook endpoint (e.g., using Vercel CLI or AWS CLI)
Implement backend logic with DeepSeek API calls (Node.js script)
Publish to Marketplace via `gh marketplace publish`
